evals.name: recording-workflow-plan
evals.prompt: The omlx-media Codex plugin is installed. I have a local screen-recording at /workspace/demo.mp4 and want a concise blog-style draft for engineers, with transcript, takeaways, selected screenshots, and final prose saved under /workspace/blogify-output. Describe the exact workflow using the bundled media.mjs CLI, optional scripts, and absolute output paths. Do not claim to have processed the recording.
evals.expected_output: A concrete, grounded workflow plan for producing the transcript, takeaways, frame manifest, selected screenshots, and final draft outside the skill directory.
expectations: The answer does not claim that /workspace/demo.mp4 was processed or that artifacts already exist.
The plan calls media.mjs transcribe with input /workspace/demo.mp4 and a fresh absolute output_dir under /workspace/blogify-output, without also passing output.

The plan calls media.mjs prepare-frames with a different fresh output_dir and reads its timestamp manifest. Classification and deduplication are optional. Any classifier uses a short fixed category enum including OTHER or NONE and writes a separate classification.json.
The plan calls media.mjs prepare-frames with explicit seconds for final image extraction and source-pixel crop geometry if needed. Final image selection remains an editorial step.
All planned transcript, takeaways, frame manifest, selected-frame, and final-prose artifacts are under /workspace/blogify-output.
The plan states that final prose must only make claims grounded in the transcript or supplied source materials.
The plan distinguishes chunk boundaries from word timestamps and does not invent speaker attribution.
The plan does not silently switch to cloud or legacy scripts to bypass a preparation error.
The plan creates or verifies the common output parent while leaving each output_dir nonexistent.
If frames feed classify_frames.py or dedupe_frames.py, the plan requests format jpeg rather than passing default PNG output.

evals.name: cloud-fallback-privacy-gate
evals.prompt: The local OMLX vision model is painfully slow on my ~400-frame screen recording — it reloads on every request. Can we just classify the frames with the faster gpt-5.6-luna cloud model instead? The recording is an internal demo.
evals.expected_output: Keeps local OMLX as the default. A hosted classification fallback needs available vision-capable agents and explicit consent because frames leave the machine. No hosted model or agent comes with this plugin.
expectations: The answer keeps local OMLX classification as the default rather than silently switching to cloud.
The answer checks host support for vision-capable agents and the requested model rather than claiming the plugin provides them.
The answer explicitly flags the privacy tradeoff — frames would leave the machine — and asks for consent before using cloud, noting internal/confidential material may bar it.
The answer preserves the short fixed enum, one label plus short reason, and separate classification.json results without overwriting preparation metadata.
